correctness.rationale: With F=(e1,2e1,3e2)⊂C², K=I, norms are 1,2,3 and F spans, so is an ordinary frame. For every t∈(0,1), c=(√t,√(1−t)/2,1/3)>0 yields Σc_i²f_if_i*=diag(t+(1−t),1)=I. Hence there is a genuine continuum of strict Parseval scalings. The published trace equality Σc_i²||f_i||²=Σd_i²||f_i||² gives ONE scalar constraint and does not force c_i²=d_i², even for unequal distinct weights. For the stated finite K-frame uniqueness criterion, let L(x)=Σx_if_if_i* into real Hermitian matrices; strict x>0 solves L(x)=KK*. If outer products independent, L injective, unique; if dependent, nonzero kernel direction z gives x±εz≥0 for sufficiently small ε, yielding distinct strict scalings. All operator identities exact, no sampled evidence.

value.rationale: A published uniqueness theorem is false even after strengthening its norm hypothesis to pairwise distinct vectors, and its main proof step is demonstrably invalid. A minimal continuum counterexample and precise strict-boundary replacement remove misleading uniqueness claims in applied K-frame scalability. Mathematical motivation is a correction of an exact literature error, rather than novelty of rank-one linear algebra.
